From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

## Preliminary points

1. **"FINAL / not to be re-opened" is the Seller's assertion, not an agreed fact.** The preamble says positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams." I have no record of this. Please confirm with Wattlebridge principals before relying on it. Until confirmed, treat every position below as open.
2. **The "market context" is Seller advocacy.** Caps of 10–20% and short claim periods are usually paired with W&I insurance. They are not a standalone market norm for a no-W&I deal. Ask whether W&I is in scope, because that changes several recommendations below.
3. **The disclosure is stale.** It speaks as at 22 September 2026, and today is 4 November 2026. We should require an updated disclosure, and any new disclosure should not cure warranties repeated at Completion.
4. **I have only the Seller's summary, not the full SPA text.** Clause references are taken from their cover note. Drafting points should be checked against the actual mark-up.
5. **The Disclosure Letter undercuts the cover note.** On Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses and DD-006, the letter's own wording shows these matters are open, not "addressed."

## Issue-by-issue

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** Without W&I, a materially higher cap (e.g. 40–50%, AUD 9.6–12m). Fundamental, tax, specific indemnity and fraud claims should sit outside this cap.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** 20% with no W&I backstop under-protects a AUD 24m deal with known open risks. If W&I is placed, we could accept a lower seller cap with buyer recourse to the policy.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis. AUD 250,000 basket, and only the excess is recoverable (deductible).
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis of about AUD 10,000, with related or series claims aggregated. A tipping basket of about AUD 120,000 (0.5%), so the full amount is recoverable once the basket is exceeded. Specific indemnities, tax, fundamental and fraud claims should be excluded from both thresholds.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** A 1% deductible combined with a 25k de minimis lets real losses fall away, particularly split items like the Sandbar renewals.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months, with "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months for general warranties, so the period covers at least two full audit cycles. Express longer periods for fundamental, tax and specific indemnity claims, and no time limit for fraud. Reverse the default so that limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** The "applies to all Claims" default silently shortens fundamental, tax and indemnity protection to 18 months.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** Cap at 100% of price (AUD 24m). Time limit of at least 6 years, aligned to NSW contract limitation periods (longer if the SPA is a deed). No de minimis or basket, and no disclosure against fundamental warranties.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing, and a 4.8m cap for "simplicity" is not acceptable.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature." No fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out so that no limitation, exclusive-remedy, non-reliance or knowledge provision applies to fraud, wilful misconduct or dishonest concealment by the Seller, its officers or its agents.
- **Recommendation: Reject and insert the carve-out.** Absent a carve-out, the drafting purports to cap the Seller's own fraud. That is commercially unacceptable, and leaving it out invites dispute over the clause's effect.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. Letter cl 1.4 denies any admission.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific disclosure only, meaning fairly disclosed with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and assess its impact, against identified warranties. No general data-room or public-records disclosure. No disclosure against fundamental, tax or specific indemnity matters. Updated disclosure at Completion should not cure breaches.
- **Recommendation: Reject general disclosure.** Wholesale disclosure of the data room effectively hollows out the warranties.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** An express statement that Buyer knowledge (actual, constructive or imputed) does not reduce claims, other than matters fairly and specifically disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** "Discoverable" plus adviser knowledge turns our due diligence into a defence for the Seller.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** "Addressed." Reasonable endeavours only. The condition is satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Letter (cl 2) confirms no consent has been given and the cl 11.3 conditions have not been evidenced.
- **Buyer should want:** A Condition Precedent requiring an unconditional written Bluefen consent under cl 11.2, or a consent whose conditions are satisfied and acceptable to the Buyer, with evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met. The Buyer should have the right to waive. A walk right or price adjustment if Bluefen terminates or re-prices. Possibly a specific indemnity or escrow for revenue loss.
- **Recommendation: Counter, and make it a hard CP.** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m). A bare consent letter with unmet conditions does not protect the contract.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion." The Letter (cl 3) confirms about AUD 3.2m is outstanding, not repaid, with no discharge of security. The facility has a change-control clause (cl 8.1).
- **Buyer should want:** Repayment at Completion from the price, treated as Debt under the debt-free/cash-free mechanics. A payoff letter before Completion. A deed of release and PPSR/security discharges delivered at Completion. Confirmation that the cl 8.1 change of control will not trigger default in the interim.
- **Recommendation: Reject the post-Completion release.** The deal is debt-free, and the security may extend to the shares or assets (see SPA-N-015). Release must happen at Completion, not on trust.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005)**
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 in Completion bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. The Letter (cl 5) is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:** All bonuses plus employer on-costs (payroll tax, super guarantee, PAYG withholding, workers' compensation) treated as Debt or Transaction Costs and deducted from the price. Alternatively, paid through payroll at Completion from Seller funds. Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** "A matter for the Seller" with nothing in the funds flow means the Company, and so the Buyer, ends up paying AUD 420k plus on-costs.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate." The Letter (cl 4) confirms transfer of SOW3 materials is conditional on full payment under DD-004 cl 7.3, AUD 180k appears open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer should want:** A CP or Completion deliverable consisting of evidence that the SOW3 fees are paid (or paid from the price) plus an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay. A broad specific indemnity covering all loss from any defect in title to SOW3 Project Materials, including third-party claims and re-development costs. The indemnity should sit outside the cap, basket and disclosure.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** The exposure is ownership of the IP, not the AUD 180k payment, so an indemnity limited to the payment misses the risk.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." The Letter (cl 6) says up to about 1,240 records were sent to an unintended external address, with access, scope and notification obligations unresolved.
- **Buyer should want:** A completed investigation before Completion, including a Notifiable Data Breaches assessment under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and OAIC notification if required. A specific indemnity for all loss, including regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, notification and remediation costs, and third-party claims. The indemnity should sit outside the cap, basket, time limit and disclosure. Add a pre-Completion conduct covenant giving the Buyer information rights.
- **Recommendation: Counter, with a specific indemnity and investigation as a CP.** Materiality is unknown, and the Seller's view that it is not expected to be material is not evidence.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals (3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course operating costs." The Letter (cl 8) says they should be read together and does not confirm they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:** Full DD-008/DD-011 review to confirm the business need, terms, termination rights and accrual status. If they were entered in contemplation of the sale or are not ordinary course, treat them as Debt or Transaction Costs, or require termination at Seller cost. Related items should aggregate for thresholds. Add a pre-Completion restriction on new or renewed contracts above a set value.
- **Recommendation: Counter or investigate.** A single AUD 330k commitment split into three related renewals warrants scrutiny, and the "ordinary course" label is unsupported.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** A single regime, with limitations applying to "all Claims of any nature" and fundamentals folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Separate tiers, each with its own cap, time limit and threshold treatment:
  - general warranties;
  - fundamental (title and capacity);
  - tax warranties and tax indemnity;
  - specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Sandbar if applicable);
  - fraud, which is uncapped.
- **Recommendation: Reject the single regime.** Merging categories is how the Seller pushes the 20% cap, 18-month limit and basket onto risks that should never carry them.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012. The Letter (cl 10) notes this is the source relied on and does not reflect any verification by the Buyer.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification: ASIC company extract, the share issue and transfer history, constitution and shareholder agreements (pre-emption rights, options, convertibles), and a PPSR search over the shares. Particular attention should go to whether Riverlark holds share security. Add fundamental title and no-encumbrance warranties. At Completion, require share certificates, signed transfers, and releases of any encumbrance.
- **Recommendation: Counter, and complete our own verification.** The register is the Seller's internal record, and outstanding Riverlark security makes an encumbrance over the shares a real risk.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, basket, general disclosure).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and super on bonuses. Cap up to 100% of price. Claim period running to the end of the relevant ATO/Revenue NSW amendment period plus a buffer (commonly 5–7 years). No basket.
  - **IP:** A higher cap and longer period than general warranties given SaaS value concentration, plus the Ironquay specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation: Reject "settled."** These terms were not agreed on our side as far as I can see, and tax and IP exposures outlast an 18-month window.

## Suggested next steps
1. Confirm internally whether any principal-level agreement was actually reached (see Preliminary point 1).
2. Decide on W&I. This drives our negotiating posture on SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-003.
3. Make these Completion conditions and deliverables: Bluefen consent, Riverlark payoff and release, Ironquay assignment, and the DD-006 investigation outcome.
4. Re-cut the funds flow to deduct the AUD 3.2m Riverlark debt, the AUD 420k bonuses plus on-costs, and any non-ordinary-course Sandbar amounts.
5. Ask for a brought-down Disclosure Letter, since the current one is dated 22 September 2026.

I can turn this into a mark-up issues list or a draft response to Seller counsel if helpful.
